title: Introduce RAG scenario lab guides and snippet garden for experimental tool-calling flows
author: Leah Kim
description:
Motivation: Teams asked for a small, opinionated playground that demonstrates progressive RAG patterns (single-shot retrieval, multi-step tool calling, and live telemetry hooks) without pulling the entire examples repo. This PR adds a lightweight 'scenario lab' in the docs site plus a compact 'snippet garden' that collects bite-sized code samples for tool-binding and telemetry instrumentation.

What this contains: - A scenario-lab guide (docs/rag/scenario-lab/index.md) with three curated scenarios: 'Search + Update', 'Form-filling with tool calls', and 'Fallback to backup model'. Each scenario includes expected prompts, sample prompts, and a deterministic verification checklist for evals. - Snippet garden (docs/snippets/snippet-garden.md) with 10 runnable snippets: 4 TypeScript, 3 Python, 2 shell examples, and an OpenAPI mock for tool stubs. Snippets emphasize safe tool-call shapes, input sanitization, and streaming-handling best practices. - Small examples folder (examples/rag/snippets/*) with a compact TS and Python binding that mirror the snippets; intentionally minimal dependencies so they can be copied into customer sandboxes. - Updated docs site config and a basic static flow diagram (docs/images/flow-diagram.svg) for the scenario-lab visual. - CI: lightweight doc linting and link checks were added to scripts/ci/validate-docs.yml to ensure snippets build in the docs runner.

Why this approach: prior quickstarts were full-stack and useful but heavy for first-time readers. The scenario-lab is designed to be a shorter intermediate step: reproducible, reviewable (can be used in quality gates), and easy to port into a codebase or a Playbook. The snippet-garden aims to centralize tiny best-practice examples so engineers don't copy entire quickstarts for a one-off pattern.

Testing and verification: - Manual walkthrough of each scenario using the local mkdocs preview. - Ran the new docs CI (link checks + snippet extraction) on the branch. - Smoke-tested TS and Python snippets against the open-source shim in examples/rag/snippets. - Verified all links and images render correctly in the built site.

Checklist: - [x] Add scenario-lab content and visuals - [x] Extract snippets into a single docs page - [x] Add minimal runnable examples (TS/Python) - [x] Add doc CI linting for snippet extraction - [x] Add Linear tickets and link SUP ticket for a known telemetry gap

Notes/Limitations: - These snippets intentionally avoid advanced stateful session code; stateful session patterns will be covered in a separate playbook. - Telemetry hooks in snippets are illustrative; production telemetry should use the full Redwood Console SDK.

Related: ENG-3281 (scenario templates), PM-421 (docs priority). For follow-ups: add runnable Docker devcontainer for each snippet and add a 'migration' page that maps snippet patterns to full quickstarts.
